At first this game is a ton of fun. And then you get to Corrective Action 20 and you're like: why tf am I even playing this. 

Rogue-lites are meant to be played in the rinse repeat style. I get that. 

However, this games specific gameplay loop is monotonous. 

Build Diversity is super narrow. Weird how a game that has untold mod potential pidgeon holes itself into only having 1 variant thats end game viable per character. 

Which brings me to character designs and skill usages. Theyre largely uninventive. Dont even get me started on Max. Super strong class with some of the worst gameplay behavior. 

There's only a few bosses total in the game. 

The barrier for entry into some of the more interesting game modes are kind of large. 

Idk the whole flow of the game felt stale, dated, and lacking in anything really engaging. 

The matchmaking system is pretty much garbage. Standard matchmaking doesnt match you with anyone. Recruiting function works for only the two basic game modes. Story and Corrective action. The other 3 game modes you cant use the recruitment function. Which is honestly just a dumb idea. Lazy devs. 

Dont get me wrong. I had some fun. For 50 hours. But I cant recommend it to anyone. There's a plethora of better options in the genre that have a more rewarding gameplay loop.

While playing this game, I had one thought repeatedly enter my brain:
What is the point of this?
I never understood what I was doing, why I was doing it, and why I was so good at doing it. The game constantly stimulates your brain with just... stuff. Stuff is always happening, you're always unlocking stuff, and you keep receiving perks that do stuff. Stuff is happening. You're doing this, now you're doing this.
What is the point of this?
Point in the vague direction of an enemy, and all your foes are gone.
Go to the shop and buy stuff with currency you don't remember collecting.
Grab a perk after clearing an area that does something.
Find a relic and add it to your collection, which also does something.
What is the point of this?

Then you have the generative machine-learning content. You can see that some of the visuals in the game are clearly made this way; mistakes that humans wouldn't make, inconsistencies across similar textures of different cosmetics for the same character that a human artist would have recycled.
What is the point of this?

Somehow, the game runs pretty smoothly, and yet stutters like crazy in simple 2-D menus. Cutscenes can play that look gorgeous, then later in the same level another plays that seems to repeatedly crash your game before unfreezing. How does this even exist?
What is the point of this?

The gameplay itself feels so polished and brimming with content, yet it all feels so pointless and hollow. The answer is there is no point. It feels like a fever dream playing this game not because it's remotely psychedelic, but because everything just feels like it was created to appeal to somebody that doesn't exist yet would have to in order for the game itself to exist. The gameplay is pointless, the progression feels pointless, the rewards are all given to you for accomplishing nothing.

20+ hours in, I can safely say this game is... enjoyable. It's fun, but not much else to say than that.

First, the roguelike elements. I can see where the replay-value for a game like this would be incredible, but at the moment its easy to get burnt out really fast. This is because every run feels the same. Sure, the stages get rearranged here and there, and there are environmental effects/hazards that have a chance of spawning in, but it still feels so samey. Every enemy can be taken out the same exact way, no strategy really needed. There's a few that have these "barriers" which are basically nonexistent because so many attacks have an AoE that completely negate them. Bosses are bullet sponges with easy to learn patterns. Most arbiters lack identity for builds. The story is nonexistent. Not much depth.

I think bosses can be easily fixed seeing as the game has verticality they don't utilize completely. Have us time our jumps more, make dodges be more integral to evading attacks, really utilize the run and gun aspect to the fullest.

Arbiters really need a rework. As of now, I honestly don't know what identity a good chunk of them are supposed to have. Let's use Rhythm as an example. Gives your dodge an AoE music blast. Ok. Gives your reload a mind-control missile, with a AoE blast at the end, alright. Gives your C an AoE music blast, mhmm. Gives your bullets a music blast that knocks back enemies and does a bit more damage. So the identity is AoE. Unoriginal, but it works (I really wish they would utilize the "rhythm" aspect more but anyways...) Sadly, a good chunk of the other arbiters have extremely similar AoE playstyles. Desire, has AoE fogs that deal damage over time. Fortune, AoE blasts from crits. Energy, probably the most underwhelming, you can build up a meter using your skills to do a... AoE blast. Gaming, AoE blast mines when you dodge. AoE here AoE there. The basic ideas are there, but they just need some refinements. Really hone in on their identities.

The characters look super fun and are probably really interesting! I'm not gonna read essays on their backstory though.

The story may be cool? I don't know what's happening, gonna be real. There's a virtual world, and a mad max world, and a virus is messing things up? I think some more compelling delivery is needed.

Regardless, I still enjoy the gameplay.

All in all, the game needs some more time to cook, some more oomph would do it some good. I hope the devs lock in, because the foundation is there. :)

Fix the god awful lag spiking and maybe I'll come back. Game is fun, combat feels great, buffs are fun to use and experiment with, modes are passable. But for the love of all that is holy, the LAG will kill you far more than your own skill will. Its not a constant lag, its a terrible spike that happens every few minutes, during which your entire game stops for a half a second. Any game like this requires precise movement and timing to dodge things, but that half second delay throws off every ounce of timing and flow. More often than not, you'll come out of it and immediately get hit several times resulting in the loss of most of your health at high level runs. It makes higher level solo runs nearly impossible. I'm on the NA Eastern server, which hovers around 15-35ms latency. So, if the devs fix the damn lag, it might actually be a great roguelike.

This game started off with a lot of promise, I mean, finally a game that wasn't focused on competitive multiplayer where we could go in and just blast away to our heart's content. But, this game is like a vacuum for wallets. While it isn't technically pay-to-win, it's got some of the most invasive and intrusive monetization I've ever seen. I mean if you're happy playing a game with "base" everything, then sure it's fine. But what if you wanted to support the game by tossing some cash at a skin... well the best skins are neck-deep in an RNG gatcha system that will bankrupt you. 

The most egregious thing of all, is the glitches and the stutters. It's a nightmare. Pure and simple. I can't overstate how much a game's reputation hinges on reliable gameplay, and this isn't it. Now, the game is sitting at just over 600 active players on Steam, the matchmaking is non-existent. Recruitment is dog-water, and unless you want to run all the content solo, you're going to be spending all your time in the lobby staring at a character you can't get skins and cool things for, because there isn't enough money in the universe for all those pulls.

I won't even give this a third chance. I'm uninstalling and moving on. This game is D. E. A. D. dead! Either the publisher or the developer doesn't care, or both... it's over, don't waste your time, just move on to the next disappointment.

i, like most other people, was not willing to give this game a genuine shot, but i'm so glad i did. 
there were so many red flags going in: i only heard about this game's existence through a discord quest, it had mixed reviews (still does as of writing this review lmao), it's a free game that launched with a paid battle pass, microtransactions, and paywalled characters, and there was a HORRIBLE stuttering issue that made the game basically unplayable. also aurora is very clearly just a gooner-bait d.va ripoff, there's that too.
however, a few updates to fix the stuttering and change the character unlock system later, and this game is honestly great.
it's hades plus marvel rivals, what's not to love? the combat system feels fantastic and super responsive, and while the perk system isn't the greatest (not a whole lot of synergy so basically no "build" potential), the character variety helps to mitigate that somewhat.
once hades 2 officially releases there's probably not gonna be a good reason to come back to this game, but until then this game is honestly a lot of fun, especially with friends.

The game has decent characters that all play somewhat differently when it comes to using abilities. Some are more unique than others, certainly. The enemies aren't all that unique, either, with floating drones that shoot you, guys with bats that charge you or guys with bats and shields. There isn't much to the game besides 'kill the enemies in an obnoxiously small arena and move to next small arena.' 

The cost for cosmetics, as I've mentioned before, are overly inflated price-wise. Where as warframes heirloom skins would be around $25 and the cheaper skins runnin around $8 with your ability to freely change their colors, this game and its devs demand $100+ to have a .125% chance for that nice skin that puts the girl in a terrible coat or a nurse outfit. 

Needless to say, the game's not as interesting as what it's based on; Risk of Rain 2.
What's even worse is that the game would run smoothly if it wasn't for the frequent micro-stutters or freezes every 10-15 seconds. Apparently, these have been issues people on the discussion board have been having and it still hasn't been addressed.

I cannot recommend the game. It's bland, and it operates poorly which damages the otherwise smooth combat.

I know the cyberpunk aesthetic has been overdone at this point. So, the biggest thing when creating a cyberpunk game or other piece of media, nowadays, is to bring something new to it that's exciting or deeply engaging/immersive. If not in the world, then with the characters. Unfortunately, this game felt like it didn't bring anything new or exciting to the cyberpunk aesthetic, or to anything at all really. The only real advantage here is that it's a free game and you may get a few hours of fun out of it.

The problems with the game start showing themselves very early however. Starting with the big one. The more powerful characters are the ones locked behind a pay wall. This already indicates the bad tendency that is to follow which is whenever they add a new character, it is added first to the shop and it will be the most powerful character which equates to pay 2 win.

There is no build diversity, only an illusion of it. The only viable builds are skill builds, any other type lags behind in damage so badly that you may as well not play.

The whole tetris mechanic to the modules is a poorly designed system. It has existed for a long time, some games have adopted it and every single time they have been worse for it because it doesn't adds anything meaningful, all it does is force players to waste time trying to figure out how to tetris the pieces for the most damage possible. This is doubly bad because if you are playing with others you either can't do that or you force everyone to wait a very long time just for you to adjust your modules.

The is very reminiscent of MMOs and mobile games with tons and tons of different windows to go multiple places claim bonus everywhere for doing A or B instead of having something simple and clean where you go to and get things there or even better, don't do that at all, let all rewards come from end of mission rewards.

Again, the game is designed to milk the players of their money overtime instead of being designed to be a good game and it is a shame because it isn't even bad, there are plenty of things to like about the game and I certainly don't mind paying for cosmetics if they are reasonably priced and I'm not being offered Pay 2 Win. As it is, give it a try, trying won't cost you anything, but I don't recomend you spending your money here. Don't reward developers who add Pay 2 Win to their games nor who take lazy/bad game design decision approaches.
